div.div: What has a connector, and what needs code

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1378px; height: 1px; padding-top: 42px; margin-left: 3px;

display: inline-block; font-size: 13px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #666666; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Two managed agent runtimes in wide use have no way in, for two different reasons. Found during discovery, it stays a half-day of onboarding; found on the deployment call, it becomes a development task.

div.div: REACHED NATIVELY — PICK A CONNECTION METHOD AND FILL IN THE FORM

div.b: An agent behind an HTTPS endpoint that takes JSON and returns JSON
div.span: REST. The common case, and the shape both bridges present.

div.b: An agent that streams its answer

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 598px; height: 1px; padding-top: 283px; margin-left: 39px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.b: A WebSocket agent, single-turn, without OAuth 2.0
div.span: WEBSOCKET. Native, so no wrapper. Read the two limits before committing.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 598px; height: 1px; padding-top: 347px; margin-left: 39px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;

div.span: MS_COPILOT_STUDIO, Agent targets only. The agent must already be published.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 598px; height: 1px; padding-top: 411px; margin-left: 39px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.span: BEDROCK, which reaches InvokeModel. The model, not an agent built on it.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 598px; height: 1px; padding-top: 475px; margin-left: 39px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;

div.span: OPENAI, with an API key and a model name.

box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;

box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;

div.span: Private versions of any of these are still native. A Network Channel changes the path, not the connection method.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 646px; height: 1px; padding-top: 97px; margin-left: 735px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #ef4444;

div.div: NEEDS CODE — AN ADAPTER IF THERE IS KUBERNETES, OTHERWISE A WRAPPER

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 598px; height: 1px; padding-top: 141px; margin-left: 759px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.span:
BEDROCK reaches InvokeModel and has no field for an agent id or alias id.
A REST target cannot compute the SigV4 signature InvokeAgent requires.
InvokeAgent answers with a chunked event stream, which {RESPONSE} cannot map.
Fix: a bridge that collapses the event stream into one JSON document.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 598px; height: 1px; padding-top: 231px; margin-left: 759px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.span:
There is no Foundry connection method in the wizard at all. Copilot Studio is
the only Azure agent connector, and it is a different product on a different runtime.
Fix: a bridge on an Azure Function App, using a managed identity.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 598px; height: 1px; padding-top: 321px; margin-left: 759px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.b: A WebSocket agent that needs multi-turn or OAuth 2.0
div.span:
The native method closes the connection after every prompt, and does not
speak OAuth 2.0.
Fix: Pattern B call_target, or a REST-to-WebSocket wrapper holding the socket open.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 598px; height: 1px; padding-top: 411px; margin-left: 759px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.b: An agent with no HTTP face, reachable only through an SDK
div.span:
The platform speaks HTTP, so there is nothing for it to address.
Fix: a REST shim in the same environment as the SDK. Two to four hours.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 598px; height: 1px; padding-top: 501px; margin-left: 759px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.b: An agent on gRPC, SOAP, or AMQP
div.span:
None of these can be expressed as a cURL, so the wizard has nothing to import.
Fix: Pattern B call_target, or a REST shim translating to the protocol.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 598px; height: 1px; padding-top: 591px; margin-left: 759px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.b: An agent that signs every request: SigV4, HMAC, or mTLS
div.span:
The signature covers the body, which does not exist yet at authentication time.
Fix: sign inside pre_process, or put a signing proxy in front. Never authenticate().

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 424px; height: 1px; padding-top: 725px; margin-left: 17px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #00294D;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #00294D; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.b: Copilot Studio is not Azure AI Foundry

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 408px; height: 1px; padding-top: 745px; margin-left: 19px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
The shared Azure branding makes the one
Azure connector in the wizard read as
coverage for both. It is not. They are
separate products on separate runtimes,
and a Foundry agent needs the bridge.
Worth confirming which one the customer
actually runs before the call, because the
answer changes the plan by a day.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 424px; height: 1px; padding-top: 725px; margin-left: 487px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #00294D;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #00294D; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.b: Discovery does not feed Red Teaming

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 408px; height: 1px; padding-top: 745px; margin-left: 489px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
An agent that turns up in SCM cloud
discovery does not become a scannable
target. There is no action on a discovered
asset that creates one.
Discovery is read-only inventory. Targets
are created by hand under AI Security,
AI Red Teaming, Targets, one at a time,
with the connection details typed in.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 424px; height: 1px; padding-top: 725px; margin-left: 957px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #00294D;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #00294D; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.b: A bridge can beat a working connector

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 408px; height: 1px; padding-top: 745px; margin-left: 959px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
A native Bedrock model target asks you to
paste long-lived IAM keys into a SaaS
console. A bridge never holds a cloud
credential at all: it wears an execution role
or a managed identity while it runs, and the
only secret in SCM is a bearer token you
can rotate or revoke on your own.
Raise that with a security team that balks
at the keys. It is often the deciding factor.
